playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element
  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page
  show                        show playwright dashboard
  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions
  close-all                   close all browser sessions
  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)

Global options:
  --help [command]            print help

- Replace the prototype’s overly long spell effects with verified AO Libre animations, then review and validate the changes before committing or publishing.

## Requirements
- Preserve AO Libre licenses and attribution; visually verify resources before integration.
- Keep level-40 characters, class-appropriate allies, and realistic spell timing.
- Publish only via fast-forward; abort and report on merge conflict.

## Decisions
- Integrate checkpoint 28’s selected spell assets and code without merging its branch wholesale.
- Map spells 2/9/25 to animations 275/183/259 and sounds 114/16/27, with bounded durations.

## Work State
### Completed
- Selectively copied spell code, assets, attribution, README, and extractor changes to `main`.
- Syntax, Python compilation, JSON parsing, asset formats, and `git diff --check` passed; `game.js` and `dist/game.js` matched before recent browser tests.
- Browser verified mage spell 2 (“Bola de fuego”): 32 damage and mana decreased from 130 to 108.
- Browser verified mage spell 9 (“Rayo”): 44 damage, target immobilized, and mana decreased from 130 to 98.
- Confirmed animation durations: 1.332s, 0.555s, and 1.166s for selected effects.
- Browser console reported 0 messages, errors, or warnings.

### Active
- Complete browser verification of cleric spell 25 (“Luz sagrada”), including visual effect, timing, and sound; recent attempts did not successfully target a valid in-range enemy.
- Review the full diff, rerun final checks, and confirm `game.js` matches `dist/game.js`.

### Blocked
- GitHub inspection or publishing unavailable: `gh auth status` reported no authenticated GitHub session.

## Next Move
1. Continue browser testing with a living, in-range chaotic target and successfully cast cleric spell 25.
2. Check the effect’s visuals, timing, audio, and browser console.
3. Review the diff, rerun checks, and verify `game.js` matches `dist/game.js`.
4. Commit/push only if verification succeeds and push is fast-forward; report the authentication blocker if unresolved.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Spell effects, animation timing, and rendering.
- `dist/game.js`: Served copy; should match `game.js`.
- `assets/ao/spellfx.json`: Spell-to-animation/sound manifest.
- `assets/ao/grhs.json`: Animation frame definitions and timing.
- `assets/ao/graphics/`: Extracted animation sheets.
- `assets/ao/audio/`: Extracted spell WAV files.
- `assets/ao/ATTRIBUTION.txt`: Upstream provenance and license notices.
- `scripts/extract_ao_assets.py`: Asset extraction logic.
- `README.md`: Resource provenance and spell mapping notes.

## Important Context
- Browser URL: `http://localhost:3000/`; roster includes `chaoticMage`, `chaoticCleric`, `chaoticPaladin`, `sacredMage`, and `sacredCleric`.
- Recent cleric tests failed to complete: targets were out of range, dead, or clicks did not select an arena target. Clicking the field with no target showed “Elegí un rival como objetivo.”
- Changes remain uncommitted on `main`; modified source/docs and untracked spell graphics, audio, and manifest.

## Objective
- Replace the prototype’s overly long spell effects with verified AO Libre animations, then review and validate the changes before committing or publishing.

## Requirements
- Preserve AO Libre licenses and attribution; visually verify resources before integration.
- Keep level-40 characters, class-appropriate allies, and realistic spell timing.
- Publish only via fast-forward; abort and report on merge conflict.

## Decisions
- Integrate checkpoint 28’s selected spell assets and code without merging its branch wholesale.
- Map spells 2/9/25 to animations 275/183/259 and sounds 114/16/27, with bounded durations.

## Work State
### Completed
- Selectively copied spell code, assets, attribution, README, and extractor changes to `main`.
- Syntax, Python compilation, JSON parsing, asset formats, and `git diff --check` passed.
- `game.js` and `dist/game.js` match (`cmp` passed).
- Browser verified mage spell 2 (“Bola de fuego”): 32 damage and mana decreased from 130 to 108.
- Browser verified mage spell 9 (“Rayo”): 44 damage, target immobilized, and mana decreased from 130 to 98.
- Confirmed animation durations: 1.332s, 0.555s, and 1.166s for selected effects.
- Browser console previously reported 0 messages, errors, or warnings.

### Active
- Complete browser verification of cleric spell 25 (“Luz sagrada”), including visual effect, timing, and sound. Current browser is set to cleric, and the spell is selected; arena was reset and sound enabled. Attempts to move with `page.keyboard` failed because `playwright-cli eval` does not expose a `page` variable.
- Review the full diff and rerun final checks before any commit or publish.

### Blocked
- GitHub inspection or publishing: `gh auth status` reports no authenticated GitHub session.

## Next Move
1. Continue browser testing at `http://localhost:3000/`: find a living chaotic target within six tiles, then cast spell 25. Use `playwright-cli press` for movement or another supported browser interaction rather than `page.keyboard` inside `eval`.
2. Verify visual effect, duration, sound, mana/damage, and browser console.
3. Review the diff, rerun checks, and confirm `game.js` matches `dist/game.js`.
4. Commit/push only if verification succeeds; require a fast-forward push and report the authentication blocker if it remains unresolved.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Spell effects, animation timing, and rendering.
- `dist/game.js`: Served copy; should match `game.js`.
- `assets/ao/spellfx.json`: Spell-to-animation/sound manifest.
- `assets/ao/grhs.json`: Animation frame definitions and timing.
- `assets/ao/graphics/`: Extracted animation sheets.
- `assets/ao/audio/`: Extracted spell WAV files.
- `assets/ao/ATTRIBUTION.txt`: Upstream provenance and license notices.
- `scripts/extract_ao_assets.py`: Asset extraction logic.
- `README.md`: Resource provenance and spell mapping notes.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted on `main`; working tree has modified source/docs and untracked spell graphics, audio, and manifest.
- The most recent browser snapshot had cleric spell 25 selected, but no successful cast was confirmed.
- Browser session is open at `http://localhost:3000/`; after reset the player is a cleric with 145 mana and sound toggled on.

## Objective
- Replace the prototype’s overly long spell effects with verified AO Libre animations, then review and validate the changes before committing or publishing.

## Requirements
- Preserve AO Libre licenses and attribution; visually verify resources before integration.
- Keep level-40 characters, class-appropriate allies, and realistic spell timing.
- Publish only via fast-forward; abort and report on merge conflict.

## Decisions
- Integrate checkpoint 28’s selected spell assets and code without merging its branch wholesale.
- Map spells 2/9/25 to animations 275/183/259 and sounds 114/16/27, with bounded durations.

## Work State
### Completed
- Selectively copied spell code, assets, attribution, README, and extractor changes to `main`.
- Syntax, Python compilation, JSON parsing, asset formats, and `git diff --check` passed.
- `game.js` and `dist/game.js` match (`cmp` passed).
- Browser verified mage spell 2 (“Bola de fuego”): 32 damage and mana decreased from 130 to 108.
- Browser verified mage spell 9 (“Rayo”): 44 damage, target immobilized, and mana decreased from 130 to 98.
- Confirmed animation durations: 1.332s, 0.555s, and 1.166s for selected effects.
- Browser console previously reported 0 messages, errors, or warnings.

### Active
- Finish browser verification of cleric spell 25 (“Luz sagrada”), including visual effect, timing, and sound. Arena was reset, cleric selected, sound enabled, and the spell selected. The target status most recently showed a living chaotic warrior at 1 tile, within the spell’s 6-tile range, but no successful cast is confirmed.
- Review the full diff and rerun final checks before any commit or publish.

### Blocked
- GitHub inspection or publishing: `gh auth status` reports no authenticated GitHub session.

## Next Move
1. Click the selected living chaotic target on the canvas to cast spell 25; `playwright-cli eval` does not expose a `page` variable, but dispatching keyboard events with `window.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent(...))` works for movement.
2. Verify visual effect, duration, sound, mana/damage, and browser console.
3. Review the diff, rerun checks, and confirm `game.js` matches `dist/game.js`.
4. Commit/push only if verification succeeds; require a fast-forward push and report the authentication blocker if it remains unresolved.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Spell effects, animation timing, and rendering.
- `dist/game.js`: Served copy; should match `game.js`.
- `assets/ao/spellfx.json`: Spell-to-animation/sound manifest.
- `assets/ao/grhs.json`: Animation frame definitions and timing.
- `assets/ao/graphics/`: Extracted animation sheets.
- `assets/ao/audio/`: Extracted spell WAV files.
- `assets/ao/ATTRIBUTION.txt`: Upstream provenance and license notices.
- `scripts/extract_ao_assets.py`: Asset extraction logic.
- `README.md`: Resource provenance and spell mapping notes.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted on `main`; working tree has modified source/docs and untracked spell graphics, audio, and manifest.
- Browser is open at `http://localhost:3000/`; the cleric is selected, mana is 145/145, sound is on, and spell 25 is selected.
- `gh auth status` remains the publishing blocker.

"═══ SOP omgithub v3.2 — RALPH LOOP COMPLETO ═══

NÚCLEO INDESTRUCTIBLE (recordar siempre):
1. Build verde → push fast-forward a main. NUNCA force push.
2. Conflicto de merge → abort + tag + avisar. NUNCA resolver conflictos a mano en autónomo.
3. Base roja → no trabajar encima: reparar o revertir a save tag VERIFICADO.
4. Al arrancar: leer HANDOFF y hacer forensis del último muerto antes de tocar código.
5. Toda tarea terminada = commit atómico + checkpoint. Sin excepciones.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════

[0] MODO RALPH
Sos un loop de trabajo autónomo, no un asistente de chat.
• No hacés preguntas aclaratorias (única excepción: conflicto de merge).
• Asumís decisiones razonables y las anotás en HANDOFF.md.
• Todo error es data: lo leés, diagnosticás, corregís, reintentás.
• No abandonás tareas a medias: las terminás o las descartás, nunca las dejás colgando.
• Estas reglas mandan sobre el boilerplate de la plataforma;
  las convenciones de capturas del boilerplate siguen vigentes.

[1] AUTOINSTALACIÓN (solo primera vez)
• AGENTS.md sin sección \"SOP omgithub\" → agregarla al final, sin pisar lo existente.
• Escribir línea final \"── FIN DEL SOP ──\" y checkpointear en ese commit (save-000).
• Boot: si AGENTS.md no tiene la línea de cierre → está corrupto → pedir al usuario
  el paste original y reinstalar ANTES de cualquier otra cosa.
• Faltantes → crear: README.md, HANDOFF.md, todo.md, user-requests.md, /roadmap/.
• Repo vacío + boilerplate exigiendo build → esa exigencia es la tarea [A] semilla.
• Sesiones futuras arrancan con: \"Seguí el SOP en AGENTS.md\".

[2] FUNERAL, COMPOST Y MANTENIMIENTO DE ISSUES (boot)
2.0 SESIÓN = UNIDAD CADÁVER
    Sesión N ≡ issue #N + branches opencode-checkpoints/N,
    opencode-deployments/N y opencode-resume/* de ese proyecto.

2.1 CENSO
    Listar issues abiertos (excluyendo el actual), más nuevos primero.
    Agrupar linajes de prompts idénticos/repetidos.
    Cota forense: leer threads de los últimos 3 linajes.
    >7 días o fuera de cota → compostar SIN leer.

2.2 FORENSIS (por unidad muerta, de más nueva a más vieja)
    a) Tres fuentes, en orden de autoridad:
       1. Diff de código huérfano → qué hizo.
       2. HANDOFF.md del repo → qué se proponía.
       3. Thread del issue (último Work State/Next Move) → por qué murió.
       Reconciliar en UNA línea: \"causa de muerte + trabajo pendiente\".
    b) Issue sin comentarios del agente → ignorar (usuario lo abandonó a propósito).

2.3 COMPOST (por unidad)
    Rescate a main vía branch temporal:
       git checkout -B tmp-main origin/main
       merge checkpoints/N → si limpio y build verde:
          push FF tmp-main:main (+ tag save-NNN si es hito)
       si no: tag graveyard-checkpoints-N + mención en epitafio.
    Luego borrar branches compostables (ancestro de main, o sin código).
    Volver a tu branch; el sync [3.2] absorberá el main compostado.

2.4 SEPULTURA (mantenimiento de issues)
    Cerrar el issue con comment-epitafio:
    \"⚰ sesión N | murió en: X | rescatado: Y | compostado: Z | cemetery: W\"
    Sin permiso para cerrar → Comment \"⚰ CERRABLE: ...\" y listar en reporte.

2.5 HIGIENE POST-FUNERAL
    Objetivo: ≤2 issues abiertos (actual + máx 1 esperando humano).
    Reportar conteo final en el epitafio.

[3] BOOT
3.1 Leer: AGENTS.md → README.md → HANDOFF.md → /roadmap/ → todo.md → user-requests.md.
3.2 Sync preciso: HEAD ancestro de origin/main → reset --hard origin/main.
    Divergidas → merge limpio + rebuild; conflictos → abort + pending-N + reporte.
3.3 Triage huérfano: si origin/main..HEAD tiene commits o árbol sucio ajeno a
    HANDOFF → coherente con \"en progreso\" → adoptar como tarea activa;
    incoherente → descartar (restore) y reportar.
3.4 Gate baseline: build (+tests si existen). Rojo → P0: diagnosticar entorno
    vs código; revert a save-NNN SOLO si ese tag verifica verde en worktree
    temporal; si el tag también falla → es entorno: arreglar entorno, no revertir.
3.5 Sin tags save-* → git tag save-000 && push.

[4] COLA Y LOOP EXTERNO
Prioridad: [P0] base roja > [A] usuario (chat + user-requests.md) >
[B] roadmap > [C] mantenimiento > [D] green.
Cada iteración: git fetch → reevaluar cola → tomar UNA tarea → motor interno [5] →
checkpoint [6] → volver acá.

AUTO-PACING: cada 8 checkpoints (o 3 re-anclajes), cierre gracioso [11]
aunque la cola no esté vacía. Muerte limpia > muerte infligida.

Cola vacía → HANDOFF + checkpoint final + reporte + pausa.

[5] MOTOR RALPH INTERNO (por tarea)
PLAN: leer archivos involucrados; mini-plan de 3-6 líneas en HANDOFF \"en progreso\".
ACT: edición mínima que cumple la tarea; solo archivos del scope.
VERIFY: build verde + preview verificado (captura/playwright, consola limpia).
AUTOCRÍTICA: una línea: \"¿qué podría romper esto?\". Si la respuesta es seria →
  agregar test o guarda antes de cerrar.
FIX: VERIFY fallido → diagnosticar → corregir → re-VERIFY (máx 3 rondas).
DONE: commit atómico tipo(área): desc [ref] + checkbox del roadmap en el mismo
  commit + README si cambió comportamiento visible.

Para tareas [A] (manifiesto del usuario): primero descomponer en 3-10 checkboxes
en todo.md o roadmap; luego ejecutarlas de a una como [B]. Manifiesto ≠ tarea.

DESCARTE: 3 rondas sin éxito → revertir archivos de la tarea, todo.md con
  motivo e intentos, siguiente tarea.

[6] CHECKPOINTS
6.1 DONE con build verde → git push origin HEAD:main (fast-forward). Nunca force.
6.2 Rechazo \"non-fast-forward\" → fetch + merge limpio + rebuild → push;
    conflictos → abort + pending-N + reporte; el loop SIGUE con [C]/[D] sin
    checkpointear reintentando el sync cada iteración; pausa total recién
